HbA1c Test: Purpose, Procedure, Normal Range & Results
May 26, 2026 - By Lupin Diagnostics
India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.

Another horrible thing was they were using the same cloth for covering for everyone that gets tucked way underneath one’s abdomen area and same was used for male and female - I was there for 1.5hours as I had been asked to wait (which was ok ) and I saw at least 7-8 patients go in and out without change of that cloth and after requesting a change of cloth they obliged and got a new cloth for my 3rd time scan in that visit. featured_reviews.name: Ekata Bavkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The actual name of this center is Seabird medicare Powai.
I had a very disappointing experience during a corporate annual health checkup at this center.

I specifically booked a Saturday slot because I am a breastfeeding mother with a 6-month-old baby, and that was the only day my husband could accompany me and take care of the baby while I completed the tests. Unfortunately, the entire process seemed poorly organized and rushed.

First, the center had confirmed a very large number of bookings (my number was 57) even though there were hardly any doctors available to conduct the tests. We waited for hours and many tests felt rushed or incomplete.

For the sonography and sono-mammography, we were told the doctor had already left and were asked to come again another day. After questioning why the appointment was confirmed in the first place, they said they would “try” to complete the test. Eventually it was done by another lady physician, which did not inspire confidence. I also asked her to check my diastasis recti condition during the scan and measure the gap. She seemed unfamiliar with the condition and simply said that it usually closes on its own instead of actually checking or measuring it during the scan. For sono mammography i was told to
come another day.

They were asking me to do 2D echo instead of TMT test because there was a lesser queue in 2D echo. However, I told them i want to do TMT test only.  During the treadmill test, the technician asked me to start running early so that my heart rate would reach the target faster and the test could finish sooner because many patients were waiting. Medical tests should not be rushed just to clear a queue.

The eye test was also concerning. I told the technician that I could not read the letters on the chart even while wearing my glasses. Instead of addressing the issue or referring me to a doctor, she asked me to consult a doctor later, but still marked the report as having no vision issues. That completely defeats the purpose of the test.

The general medical consultation was extremely brief. The doctor only asked about medications and family history and then asked me to leave.

The only test that seemed properly conducted was the Pap smear, which was performed by a qualified gynecologist.

Overall, we spent nearly 3 hours there and most of the experience felt rushed, poorly coordinated, and lacking proper medical supervision. For something as important as a health checkup, patients deserve better organization and qualified staff.

I hope the management improves scheduling, ensures doctor availability, and maintains proper standards for medical testing.

HbA1c Test: Purpose, Procedure, Normal Range & Results
May 26, 2026 - By Lupin Diagnostics
India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.
